claims.text: The proposed predictive approach is a neural network with two hidden layers and 128 neurons per layer.
The neural network is trained using mean squared error, Adam, and a learning rate of 0.001.
A training dataset includes conductivity measurements from bulk HfNbTaTiZr with 0 and 1 wt.% oxygen.
The training dataset covers temperatures of 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Oxygen content can be used as a model input or mediator for predicting conductivity in bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The neural network will learn relationships among oxygen content, temperature, and conductivity.
Nonlinear interactions and correlations involving oxygen content and temperature are not easily captured by existing analytical models.
Accounting for these nonlinear interactions and correlations will improve conductivity-prediction accuracy.
The model will achieve a conductivity MAE below 0.1 W/m-K over 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The neural network will predict conductivity more accurately than existing analytical approaches.
The proposed applicability range includes bulk HfNbTaTiZr specimens containing 0–1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed applicability range includes specimen sizes from 1 to 10 mm.
Model accuracy may depend on the quality and quantity of training data.
The model may not generalize to oxygen contents outside 0–1 wt.%.
Failure to reduce MAE by at least 15% relative to existing analytical approaches would falsify the hypothesis.
